title: Complex Numbers
prerequisites: Plotting points in the Cartesian plane.

topics.title: Complex Numbers and Their Algebra
topics.quick_summary: A complex number has the form a + ib where i = √−1, and complex numbers are added, multiplied and divided using ordinary algebra together with i² = −1.
topics.real_life: Alternating-current circuits are analysed with complex impedance, because it captures both the size and the timing of a signal in one number.

detailed.definition: A complex number is of the form z = a + ib, where a is the real part, b is the imaginary part and i = √−1 with i² = −1. The conjugate of z is z̄ = a − ib and the modulus is |z| = √(a² + b²).
detailed.key_idea: Complex numbers exist so that every quadratic has roots. Once i is admitted, the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra guarantees that every polynomial of degree n has exactly n roots.
detailed.working_principle: Division is carried out by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, which makes the denominator real because (a + ib)(a − ib) = a² + b².
applications: Powers of i cycle with period 4: i, −1, −i, 1.
Roots of a quadratic with negative discriminant are complex conjugates.
The Argand plane represents a + ib as the point (a, b).

points: i = √−1, i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁴ = 1; powers repeat with period 4.
z = a + ib; conjugate z̄ = a − ib; modulus |z| = √(a² + b²).
z · z̄ = a² + b² = |z|², which is always real and non-negative.
Divide by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate.
Complex roots of a real polynomial always occur in conjugate pairs.
mistakes: Treating i as an ordinary variable and forgetting i² = −1.
Comparing two complex numbers as greater or less; they cannot be ordered.
topics.memory_hook: 'i squared is minus one' — and the powers of i cycle every four.
topics.advanced: Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ unites exponentials with trigonometry, and at θ = π gives e^(iπ) + 1 = 0, linking the five most important constants in mathematics in a single equation.

formulas.name: Modulus and Conjugate
formulas.variables: z = a + ib, a = real part, b = imaginary part.
formulas.when_to_use: For division, rationalising and finding the distance of a point from the origin in the Argand plane.
formulas.common_mistakes: Forgetting to change the sign of only the imaginary part when conjugating.
formulas.shortcut: |z| is just the distance formula applied to the point (a, b).

formulas.name: Roots of a Quadratic with D < 0
formulas.variables: a, b, c = coefficients, with b² − 4ac < 0.
formulas.when_to_use: When the discriminant is negative and complex roots are required.
formulas.common_mistakes: Leaving a negative quantity under the root instead of extracting i.
formulas.shortcut: The two roots are always conjugates of each other.
